products.body_html:
The third volume of this six-part collection of annotated, never-before-seen sketches by Prince Valiant creator Hal Foster continues the series’ project of revealing in intimate detail the act of creating this landmark comic strip.

Part sketchbooks, part biography, part tutorial, part memoir—Hal Foster’s Prince Valiant Sketchbooks are an unprecedented revelation of Foster’s personal life and creative process during his final nine years on the strip, as well as a fascinating look behind the curtains as Foster coached and interacted with his chosen successor: John Cullen Murphy. Beautifully, meticulously designed and produced with the full participation of the Murphy family, this series is a testament to author and Prince Valiant historian Brian M. Kane’s research prowess and determination to bring Foster’s aesthetic and storytelling strategies to light.

Over the course of these volumes, Kane annotates with painstaking clarity and thoroughness 366 penciled layout pages, 40-character sketches, and 577 text pages of Foster’s descriptions of each panel. Also featured are an additional 143 pieces of art, mostly by Foster, 100 photographs detailing his life and career, and 123 personal letters and notes, all adding immeasurably to this exploration of Foster’s life and art, as well as his collaboration with Murphy.
products.title: Hal Foster's Prince Valiant Sketchbooks: An Illustrated Memoir: Volume 3

Celebrate Jaime Hernandez's iconic women's-wrestling extravaganza with a super soft, heavyweight cotton tee! Printed by hand right here in Seattle, sizes range from Small to 3XL.

products.body_html: Straight from the Unifactor, it's your favorite generic anthropomorph...in accessory form! Featuring Jim Woodring's beloved Frank, this 1" enamel pin has a rubber push back and is the perfect accompaniment to your favorite bag, shirt, lanyard, and more. Only at Fantagraphics!
products.title: Jim Woodring's Frank Enamel Pin

products.body_html: Funny animal comics fans will rejoice over this all-new one-shot comic book from the mighty pen of Noah Van Sciver! Meet Hefty Duck, a hyperbolic, paranoid narcissist! Will he find a job in this economy? Also introducing: the criminal rat brothers! Dinky Doormouse! Duncan the rabbit! In the grand tradition of Fritz the Cat, Disney Ducks, Pogo and more, Van Sciver makes the comic bookstore safe once again for anthropomorphic hijinx!
products.title: Animal Comix and Stories #1

products.body_html:
A surreal Nordic giallo set in corporate Scandinavia in the 1980s, perfect for fans of David Lynch, Junji Ito, and Daniel Clowes’s Like a Velvet Glove Cast In Iron.

A terrible explosion occurs at a factory; the injured are evacuated. The worst is averted, but this industrial accident triggers a series of macabre events. The top executives who were touring the factory that day are now the targets of numerous assassination attempts. After each attack, a white car speeds off. Its trail disappears at the edge of a forest, a dark alley, or a vacant lot. The mystery remains unsolved. While contracts continue to be signed in the corridors of power, an investigation is launched, private security agents are hired, and former rock stars are called in to help. Everything is shrouded in secrecy and conspiracy. White Volvo unfolds in a bygone 1980s Scandinavia; a world of businessmen sporting forced smiles, tinted aviator sunglasses, ties that hang below the belt, bald heads, and long hair.

Following the acclaimed Spa, Erik Svetoft's new graphic novel is a thriller, as gripping as it is hilarious. Who is driving the white Volvo? While horror is still present, it manifests itself in a grotesque depiction of neoliberal society, inherited from a magical realism that flirts with the occult. The author's virtuoso artwork is combined with caustic writing that mimics the excesses of bureaucratic jargon. A mercilessly surreal and absurd thriller.
products.title: White Volvo

products.body_html:
Scrooge McDuck—out of date? Never! In a wild new graphic novel, the cantankerous gold-rush tycoon vows to get as rich through cryptocurrency and influencer culture as he has through old-time mining and treasure hunting! How many ways can this go wrong?

Compared to the tech world's giga-mega-billionaires—especially that up-and-coming blowhard bro, Carsten Duck—old-school tycoon Scrooge McDuck might seem hopelessly out-of-date. But he's not going to stay that way!

In an all-new feature-length graphic novel by Julien "Jul" Berjeaut and Nicolas Keramidas, Scrooge's quest to be Duckburg's influencer king of crypto is on… and no (literal) duckface or tie-in stunt can be left behind, even when the Beagle Boys turn tech-bros too—and empty Scrooge's Money Bin in a whirlwind cyberattack!

Can Gyro Gearloose help Scrooge save the McDuck millions? Or will Scrooge take a dive in virtual cash without a crash helmet?
products.title: Uncle Scrooge: Bitquack Backlash

products.body_html:
Experience Scrooge McDuck’s and Flintheart Glomgold’s most epic-length showdown, full of treasure and traps—then travel to the Klondike for the start of an all-new miniseries, “The McDuck Journals!”

Fantagraphics’ first four issues of the Uncle Scrooge Disney Legacy comic books come together in one amazing volume! Uncle Scrooge #461-464 are collected here, packed with thrills, chills… and a Money Bin full of extras!

In our awesome 120-page title story, Scrooge McDuck’s ruthless rival, second-richest tycoon Flintheart Glomgold, returns to Duckburg—claiming he’s reformed for good, and inviting Huey, Dewey, and Louie to Ophir, Glomgold’s luxurious new island estate! But since when was Glomgold a good guy… or a big spender? Soon Scrooge’s nephews are trapped—and their trail of trouble points Scrooge and Donald Duck to the Amazon and the legendary lost city of Z!

But the show isn’t over! In “The McDuck Journals: The Klondike Years,” Scrooge himself narrates untold 1890s tales of his mining days in the Yukon! A rogues’ gallery including Soapy Slick, the Beagle Boys, Cobalt Blue, and Septimus Sharky are all set on Scrooge’s path by a mystery tycoon who wants to force him back to Scotland—for good!

Featuring extra Carl Barks gags, a complete cover gallery, an interview with the talents behind the stories, and a new “Sinister Secret” bonus scene making its debut in this volume, the first Scrooge Timeless Tales volume is a rushing river of adventure!
products.title: Uncle Scrooge Timeless Tales: Flintheart Glomgold's Sinister Secret

products.body_html:
There’s something aspirational in the inevitable force of the feline will, as evidenced in this delightful gift book from best-selling cartoonist—and cat lover—Jeffrey Brown.

“Today I am going to sit on your desk and knock stuff off. Try and stop me.” So begins Jeffrey Brown’s utterly charming ode to the independent personalities, inquisitive natures, cleanliness, stubbornness, and displays of affection that cats deign to share with their human guardians. This delightful cartoon book serves both as an inspiration in the way a cat never shies from taking agency in any situation—and a cautionary tale in what happens when someone or something is free to rampage around and leave chaos in their wake. Most of all, it’s a hilarious reminder of why so many of us identify as cat lovers, making it a perfect gift for the cat lover in your life.
products.title: Try and Stop Me

products.body_html:
A Cronenbergian conflation of a love story and body horror as an HR manager and her girlfriend get entangled with a man who discovers a strange phenomenon in his apartment.

Acclaimed cartoonist Bhanu Pratap (NOW, Cutting Season) delivers the first long form work of his still-ascending career. Pratap seamlessly blends his core obsessions—distortion, abstraction, romance, sex, body horror, isolation, violence, color, humor, and a seductive sense of design and composition—into a thrilling love story about an HR manager and her girlfriend who get sucked into the life of a young man experiencing a terrifying phenomenon that traps him in his apartment. When Brina attempts to visit the man at home after he stops showing up at work, she discovers something way beyond her pay grade. The World Is An After-Image is simultaneously both the most vividly accessible work of Pratap’s career, while also remaining true to his distinctively haunting and romantic artistic vision.

The first 250 of The World is an After-Image include a free bumper sticker while supplies last!
tags: the world is an after image
products.title: The World Is An After-Image

products.body_html:
Sherlock Holmes, Hercule Poirot, Philip Marlowe—and Nestor Burma! Fantagraphics presents the first episode of Tardi & Malet's classic mystery series starring the iconic Parisian private eye, set in atmospheric, WWII-era France.

"120 Rue de la Gare." These are the mysterious last words spoken to detective Nestor Burma by his partner, as he is gunned down by an unknown assailant at the Perrache train station in Lyon. The only problem — no such address exists! This fateful moment kicks off a beguiling mystery, in which Paris' ace P.I. must navigate the mean streets of Nazi-occupied France, contend with friends and friendly foes alike, and muster all of his wits to solve the most bewildering case of his storied career!

Fantagraphics is thrilled to resurrect Nestor Burma, the iconic noir series by legendary French creators Léo Malet and Jacques Tardi. This first installment features all the hallmarks of a classic detective yarn: a gritty setting, a cast of colorful characters (including a renowned pearl thief, a crooked cop, a dogged newsman, a dazzling femme fatale), a deliciously confounding mystery rife with twists and turns and plenty of red herrings — and at the heart of it all, Nestor Burma, the world-weary, wisecracking, pavement-pounding, quintessentially Parisian gumshoe.

Originally created in 1943, and adapted into comics in 1982, Nestor Burma is France's most enduring literary detective. The Riddle of 120 Rue de la Gare is the first of three planned volumes to present Tardi and Malet's dynamic collaboration to American fans of crime fiction and masterful cartooning.
products.title: The Riddle of 120 Rue de la Gare: A Nestor Burma Mystery

products.body_html:
An anthology of comics journalism about the Gisèle Pelicot mass rape trial in France that shocked and inspired people across the world, sparking movements against sexual violence and the social causes of violence that harm all of us.

"I saw these women, these mothers, these sisters testify in court that their son, their father, their brother, their husband was an exceptional man. I had the same at home." —Gisèle Pelicot

Fifty-one rapists. One victim. An open trial. In 2024, Gisèle Pelicot's story dominated the global media: a woman whose husband of 50 years drugged her for a decade and invited men to their home to rape her, repeatedly. Gisèle's courage in the face of relentless adversarial scrutiny during the trial made her a cultural icon across the world. Critically, the men on trial are not monsters. They are ordinary men: good fathers, good husbands, good men. Why did they rape Gisèle Pelicot?

Twenty-three renowned European cartoonists, paired with experts, tell the story of the trial, interspersed by investigations into the social factors that shape our evolving understanding of gender-based and sexual violence. This is a meticulous recounting of the horrific events that led up to the 16-week trial, and a brutally honest examination of the banality of violence. It's also a tribute to the nerve and courage of Gisèle Pelicot, who stayed resolute throughout the judicial ordeal. Its creators call on everyone to join against gender-based and sexual violence: it's up to all of us.

Artists included in the book: Lucie Albrecht, Alfred, Nine Antico, Bobika, Patricia Bolaños, Sylvain Bordesoules, Anjuna Boutan, Coco, Tiffany Coope, Deloupy, Marie Dubois, Florence Dupré la Tour, Alix Garin, Hippolyte, Léa Hybre, Kokopello, Carole Lobel, Carole Maurel, Sole Otero, Claire Roquigny, Charlotte Rotman, Lili Sohn, Chloé Wary, Quentin Zuttion.
tags: a hymn to life shame has to change sides
journalism and visual essays by 23 international cartoonists
products.title: The Pelicot Rape Trial: Journalism and Visual Essays by 23 International Cartoonists

products.body_html:
The second monumental volume collecting Barry Windsor-Smith’s comics at Marvel includes stories starring Machine Man, Daredevil, and The Thing.

The comics featured in American Dreamer, Fantagraphics' second volume (of three) collecting all of Barry Windsor-Smith’s work at Marvel, provides a stark contrast between the artist’s early experimentation on Daredevil under the influence of Jim Steranko and Jack Kirby and the full-blown, unique storytelling brilliance displayed a few years later on Machine Man and his later return to Daredevil. Windsor-Smith’s plotting and powerful visuals evoking the circuitry-born identity of Machine Man are unforgettable, but this volume also sees the full emergence of BWS the writer with the legendary Thing story he fully scripted and drew for Marvel Fanfare. Also: Marvel editor Archie Goodwin’s 1981 interview reveals insights into Windsor-Smith’s life and art, and comics historian and editor Jon B. Cooke’s continuing biography covers the artist's time on Conan the Barbarian.
products.title: The Marvel Creator Collection No. 3: "American Dreamer" Barry Windsor-Smith at Marvel Vol. 2

products.body_html:
The story of a photojournalist in Gaza and what he owes to those he photographs.

Giulio, an Italian photojournalist, is tasked with entering Gaza to capture the face of genocide. At first, he is detached, hunting for the glory of a Pulitzer, and the perfect shot of despair that will win it for him. As the days drag on and the atrocity persists, he's forced to reflect on the faces that look back.

Across the ruined expanse of Gaza, he chronicles the stories of Palestinian survivors. He meets dance instructors who resist the physical and spiritual assault of the Israeli operation through defiant joy. He converses with a fatigued Palestinian doctor as they discuss choked humanitarian supply lines through the filter of a cigarette.

Writer-artist duo Marco Sonseri and Gian Luca Doretto tell a powerfully humane story that emphasizes not only the human cost of the ongoing genocide, but the complicity that perpetuates it. Told through a visually timeless figurative stylization recalling traditional masters like John Severin and Joe Kubert, the loudest thing in Gaza is not the bombs, but the roar of silence from the international community—their stubborn, deathly denial. In the time of genocide, silence kills. The only shield against annihilation is speaking out, no matter the cost. The Darkest Night in Gaza demands a glimmering dawn that may never arrive.
products.title: The Darkest Night in Gaza: A Graphic Novel

products.body_html:
A poignant work of graphic medicine, Over My Dead Body explores Kriota Willberg’s journey of healing, artistic expression, and scientific study—all through the lens of anatomy.

It all started with a dead bullfrog. When Kriota was 11, her professor father brought home a preserved frog for the two of them to dissect. Instead of being grossed out, she was delighted to learn about the frog’s anatomy. This strange but illuminating experience sparked what would become her lifelong obsession with anatomy, which she would explore through dance, massage, illustration—and hands-on scientific study in cadaver labs.

For cartoonist Kriota Willberg, anatomy is not only a fascinating scientific perspective, but also a lens through which she can explore health, relationships, and artistic expression. Throughout, Willberg’s highly detailed sketches of cadavers reveal the beauty in the structure of our bodies. And her practices of dance and meditation, getting in touch with her body, help her heal from past sexual trauma.

Philosophical, poignant, and playful, Over My Dead Body is a life-affirming memoir about the author’s curiosity and reverence for the human body—dead and alive.
tags: over my dead body dissecting my life
products.title: Over My Dead Body: Dissecting My Life

products.body_html:
Equal parts interrogation and ode, a profound and urgent meditation on the legacy of George Orwell, the cartoonist’s connection to his works, and their ongoing political relevance.

From 1984 to Animal Farm, from his writing on (and participation in) the Spanish Civil War to his essays on language—out of a refined upbringing of classical British manners, George Orwell became arguably the most enduring political writer of the 20th century. Now, some 75 years later, the cartoonist Gina Siciliano reckons with his legacy with a finely nuanced attention and rigor. Immaculately researched and lovingly rendered, this graphic essay contemplates all facets of Orwell: a prophetic writer of dystopias, eager revolutionary, sensitive humanist, and product of empire beholden to chauvinist thinking.

Siciliano also traces the development of her own political consciousness. From the earliest flirtations with leftist politics as a young Crass-loving misfit punk to a working-class artist who never takes her values for granted. Where Orwell imagines the broad sweep of dystopia, Siciliano thoughtfully captures the gloom and luminance of modern times. Orwell and Me is a rewarding rumination on both Orwell and his relevance to our dystopian times.
tags: orwell and me a comparative political memoir
products.title: Orwell and Me: A Comparative Political Memoir

products.body_html:
A career-spanning collection of scathing satirical comics strips and cartoons by the inimitable Drew Friedman, aka the “Vermeer of the Borscht Belt.”

Drew Friedman’s Misanthropic Funnies, featuring a foreword by cartoonist Noah Van Sciver, presents an omnibus of comic strips, cartoons, book/comic book/magazine and CD cover art, posters, ads, trading cards, sketches, character designs, portraits, and new and previously unpublished art. From RAW and National Lampoon to Mineshaft and The New Yorker, this anthology covers forty years of artwork, 1987–2027.

For years, acclaimed artist Drew Friedman has chronicled an oddball, alternate history of American pop culture, where forgotten character actors, old Jewish comedians, comic book artists, and liver-spotted elevator operators are afforded the spotlight over Hollywood starlets and heartthrobs.?Misanthropic Funnies continues Drew’s life mission, with scathing comic strips such as “The 10 Least Powerful People in L.A.,” “Shows You Won’t Be Seeing This Year,” “Retired Elevator Men on JFK,” “From Hitler To Hollywood,” and many others, and unforgettable characters such as Thunderclap E. Neuman, Cole Slaw, A. Schmuck, and Ed McLoins.
products.title: Misanthropic Funnies: An Anthology of Comic Art 1987-2027

products.body_html:
Fan-favorite talents—fronted by writer/artist Andrea “Casty” Castellan—pit Mickey and Goofy against legendary archenemies including Pegleg Pete, the Rhyming Man, and the Beagle Boys!

Fantagraphics’ first four issues of the Mickey Mouse Disney Legacy comic books are gathered in one thrilling volume! The rumors are true… Mickey is again an epic hero with an incredible rogues’ gallery! Now Mickey Mouse #331-334 come together in one book, pulsing with adventure and wild laughs!

In our title story, the Phantom Blot conquers Mouseton with an army of its own citizens—cloned! Then in “Ripples in Time,” that dastardly verse-spouting spy, The Rhyming Man, will travel to 2053 A.D. to steal hi-tech from the future… unless Mickey and Time Police Agent Uma get there first! Finally “The Amorphium Menace” is a shapeshifting alien glob that can become whatever it wants—and Pegleg Pete knows just what to morph it into!

Feature-length Mickey tales by Andrea “Casty” Castellan and Francesco Vacca, all new to North America, are bookended by shorter comedies and rare Golden Age reprints. The whole gang’s here: from Minnie and Goofy to Bowery-boy Butch, genius Dr. Einmug, and—in an invasion from Duckburg—the Beagle Boys!

Featuring bonus extras for completist collectors, this Timeless Tales volume is one that no Mouse fan should miss!
products.title: Mickey Mouse Timeless Tales: The Phantom Blot's Double Revenge

products.body_html:
Collects the first six issues of the fourth, and current, volume of the Love and Rockets comic book series (2016–2018) and features the continuing adventures of Maggie, Ray, Hopey, Luba, and Fritz, as well as new adventures starring twins Rosy and Baby, Tonta, Judy Fair, Frank Lopez, and—Princess Anima?!

Love and Rockets Vol. IV Book One collects the first six issues of the new, magazine-sized comic book just as they are—with Jaime’s and Gilbert’s storylines as intertwined segments. Published 2016–2018, this is the continuation of the 40+ year series fans have been clamoring for! While portions have appeared as standalone graphic novels, much of this material has yet to be reprinted. In this book, when a Hoppers punk show reunion throws Maggie, Hopey, and the rest of the Locas/Locos gang back together, glimpses of their past helps them move into their future. Plus: in further installments of Jaime’s SF serial, Lumina and Isla search their galaxy for the See Stone, aided by the powerful and mysterious Princess Anima. Meanwhile, Gilbert’s storyline concerns the break-up of Fritz’s and Pipo’s marriage—just as Fritz reconnects with her teen twin daughters, Baby and Rosy, and grapples with aging as an artist. And, in one of the most moving chapters in the Palomar saga, Luba and her grown children reconnect at Guadalupe’s wedding. Here comes the groom … Steve?!
products.title: Love and Rockets Vol. IV Book One

products.body_html:
The true story of an anticolonial movement, a political hope dashed, and an ordinary woman who became a firebrand for Puerto Rican independence — told in breathtaking woodcut.

In 1954, four Puerto Rican Independence activists stormed the Capitol, armed with pistols, demanding liberation for their people. But before they were pariahs of white America, before they were symbols of liberation, they were ordinary people. Told in gorgeous woodcuts that imbue the narrative with a quality that is both tactile and mythic in essence, this graphic narrative explores the extraordinary life of one ordinary woman: Lolita Lebrón.

Through rich, expressionistic imagery, Lolita’s life of migration and toil is laid bare. While factory foremen shout in hostile, foreign tongues, there’s talk of revolution in snug tenements where children run and play. Interspersed are sketches of Puerto Rican history and folklore, carving a defiant line from the personal to the political.

The brilliant follow-up to John Vasquez Mejias’s Eisner-nominated debut woodcut graphic novel, The Puerto Rican War—the original prints of which reside in the permanent collection of The Metropolitan Museum of Art—Lolita Lebrón: Puerto Rican Revolutionary is both an urgent call for and a compelling history of bravery and women’s radical resistance in the face of violent imperialist ambition.
products.title: Lolita Lebrón: Puerto Rican Revolutionary

products.body_html:
Blankets meets Pet Sematary in the long-awaited comeback from the author of The End of the Fucking World and I Am Not Okay With This, a crossover horror story set in the early ’90s, in which a desperate suburban teen brings his mother back from the dead.

Josh Mort is a 16-year-old nerd living in a small American town in the early 1990s. He lives with his checked-out father and his younger brother, Pete. He has a best friend, Greta, who he secretly loves, and a serial bully, Corey, who won't leave him alone. His pregnant mother, Lindsay, died the year before, officially in a car accident, but her past suggests otherwise.

One day, while trying to bury his cat (run over by his drunken father) in the woods behind the local cemetery, Josh discovers a mysterious old book, which turns out to be a book of black magic containing various spells, including one on how to revive the dead... Ex Utero, dripping in grunge atmosphere, mines familiar thematic territory for fans of Forsman’s previous bestsellers: raw adolescence, young romance, slowly building tension, and those small cracks in reality that make everything more and more unsettling—all sprinkled with a perfectly controlled touch of the fantastic. Forsman is a master of his craft, and he proves it a little more with each new book. Ex Utero is Forsman's most accomplished work to date, a horror story that masks an exploration of personal family trauma and how to reconcile one’s complex relationship with a parent after their death.
tags: i am not okay with this
the end of the fucking world
products.title: Ex Utero

products.body_html:
David is caught between childhood and adolescence, and his end-of-year play will be an opportunity to step offstage into adulthood...
David is 14—an age at which kids want to be grown-ups but, somehow, without changing too much, too soon. Taking part in the end-of-year play, in which he will play Aslan, the wise and powerful lion who created the world of Narnia, marks a subtle turning point. It’s a chance to step into the adult world—or at least a rehearsal for it. It is the moment when the games of childhood lose their appeal, when the playground becomes too small, when we grow a few inches taller. It is the moment of first loves and first secret beers. It is the moment when, off stage and away from prying eyes, we prepare for the role of "grown-up" that we will soon play.
Adding subtle touches with his signature precision, Jon McNaught once again manages to paint a reality that is both indescribable and universal, using sublime words and images to capture the rhythm of nature, the passage of time, adolescence, boredom, and beauty, transforming the ordinary into the extraordinary. A successor to Richard McGuire or Chris Ware, McNaught's seemingly insignificant moments transport us into the gentle melancholy of our everyday lives.
products.title: Deep Magic

products.body_html:
A wagon train of pioneers heading west finds themselves trapped in a Rocky Mountain “Bermuda Triangle.”

Steven Weissman’s long-awaited graphic novel Black Feather Valley, his first in over a decade, feels like the culmination of a lifetime of experience as a father and son, and as one of the most fiercely independent and singular cartoonists of his generation. From youthful themes of coming-of-age and falling in love, to midlife concerns of being a parent and letting go as the child enters adulthood, Black Feather Valley mines a treasure of feeling and emotion in this somewhat fantastical adventure of settlers in the old west who find themselves lost in a mysterious valley filled with wolves the size of horses, crows the size of buffalo, a clan of molepeople, and much more.

Weissman channels inspiration like Max Fleischer’s Popeye the Sailor Meets Sindbad the Sailor, Turok comic books and other Dell western and animal comics, Steinbeck’s The Red Pony and East of Eden, as well as the paintings of Charles M. Russell, to create this curiously affecting and utterly unique work of graphic brilliance. Always a singular stylist in comics, Black Feather Valley is a showcase for Weissman’s distinctive cartooning language, his innate storytelling skills, and an acute sense of comic timing. Weaving a lovable cast of characters both human and animal (no one in comics does horses better than Weissman) through a series of vignettes that tell the individual stories of the cast while also propelling the wagon train’s desperate need to escape the valley, Black Feather Valley is pure comic book fun, with a heart of gold.
products.title: Black Feather Valley

products.body_html:
Revolutionaries collects the most politically galvanizing stories by the subversive comix artist, social activist, and outlaw biker Spain Rodriguez.

In Revolutionaries, Spain illustrates the lives of some of great historical figures who fought for revolution and independence, including Nestor Makhno, Bernardo Galvez, plus contemporary heroes and villains in the fight for democracy. He also recounts his role in the sexual revolution of the 1960s with autobiographical strips from the East Village Other, Hustler, and Sleazy Scandals of the Silver Screen, exercising the complete artistic freedom those periodicals afforded him. Plus graphic short stories of revolutionary Yiddish entertainers and activists in the Lower East Side that first appeared in Jewish Currents, in collaboration with Jewish scholar Joel Schechter.

Spain Rodriguez absorbed revolutionary and military history throughout his life and showcased his eclectic knowledge in the stirring tales of freedom fighting that appear in this volume, from ancient historical times to 20th and 21st century political machinations. This volume collects stories from Arcade, Anarchy, Commies From Mars, Two-Fisted Tales, and Death Rattle and other comix titles from his six -decade career.
products.title: Revolutionaries: Spain Vol. 4

products.body_html:
The Eisner Award-winning graphic history of women’s suffrage in the U.S. returns in paperback, with additional commentary about the author’s personal experiences of the book’s release, the recent devastating attacks on voting rights in America—and how we can organize to continue the fight.

In Suffrage Song, cartoonist Caitlin Cass traces women’s fight to vote in the U.S., a fight that waged over a century, from the 1848 Seneca Falls Convention to the Voting Rights Act of 1965.

Cass takes a critical, intersectional approach to the history of voting rights — celebrating the pivotal, hard-fought suffrage battles while also illuminating the problematic decisions that haunt the movement. She explores the multigenerational arc of the struggle, humanizing key historical figures from the movement’s early days (Susan B. Anthony, Frances Watkins Harper), to the dawn of the “New Women” (Alice Paul, Mary Church Terrell), to the Civil Rights era (Fannie Lou Hamer, Ella Baker). Additionally, this book highlights less chronicled figures such as Zitkala-Ša and Mabel Ping Hua-Lee, whose stories reveal the complex racial dynamics at the heart of this history.

Released to wide acclaim in 2024, Suffrage Song has become an essential document of suffrage history, whose themes and lessons echo powerfully into the present. The paperback edition will feature a new chapter, in which the author reflects on the surreal nature of releasing a politically charged book amidst America’s fascist takeover, documents the recent devastating attacks on voting rights in the country, and encourages readers to get involved through organizing and activist efforts.
tags: suffrage song the haunted history of gender race and voting rights in the us
products.title: Suffrage Song: The Haunted History of Gender, Race and Voting Rights in the U.S.

products.body_html:
A sensitive masterpiece from Japan’s most prominent creator of LGBTQ+ manga—this collection includes the third and fourth volumes of the acclaimed Wandering Son series in a newly designed paperback edition.

Ariga Makoto, another boy who wants to be a girl, joins Shuichi’s and Yoshino’s friend group, which already includes the intense Chiba Saori and the cheerful Sasa Kanako. Maho and Shuichi foray into the world of tween modeling, meeting idol Maiko, Suehiro Anna, and Satoh Tamaki. But when Yoshino’s and Shuichi’s cross-dressing comes to light at school, everything changes. In the next chapter, Yoshino unhappily dresses like a girl, and Shuichi and Makoto talk about how Makoto isn’t perceived as a girl as easily. Maho befriends the models, who begin to hang out at the Nitoris’ home. Then, love triangles throw everyone’s relationships into disarray. Will they be restored in the next volume, in … gulp, junior high?

Written and drawn by one of today’s most critically acclaimed creators of manga, Shimura Takako (Even Though We’re Adults), portrays Shuishi and Yoshino’s journey with affection, sensitivity, and gentle humor as they are figuring out their respective genders and take tentative, age-appropriate steps toward transitioning. This new paperback edition collects the third and fourth volumes of Wandering Son (which has been adapted into an anime of the same name, currently available on Crunchyroll).
products.title: Wandering Son: Volumes Three & Four

products.body_html:
In the second installment of the acclaimed manhwa romantic dramedy series, Arisa and Jun grow closer, make intriguing new acquaintances, and discover the enticing wonders of Gyeongseong, the vibrant capital city of South Korea in the 1930s.

In Gyeongseong, Arisa and Jun’s story is heating up — literally, as the city is experiencing a sweltering heat wave! While some refreshing bingsu (Korean shaved ice) cools things down, the fiery connection between the city girl and the country boy continues to blaze. The second volume of Lovers of the Empire teases out Arisa and Jun’s budding relationship, and enriches their story by introducing several new captivating characters. Meet Kim Hwajeong: beautiful, smart, and sweet — but mysteriously expelled from school. The cocky Cheolsu takes Jun to the Willow Tree, a Japanese teahouse with a tantalizing twist that will make our country boy blush. And Arisa makes fast friends with the spitfire Mari Bak, a girl from the countryside just like Jun, but who is far bolder than he could ever be.

Yet, a chance encounter threatens to dash all of these delightful escapades. Handed a secret note with a call to action, Jun has a choice to make that could forever change his fate in the capital.

In Lovers of the Empire, Yudori conjures a coming-of-age love story, in a lush period setting — with two winsome characters at its heart.
products.title: Lovers of the Empire: Vol. 2

products.body_html:
Moto Hagio’s foundational shojo Poe Clan series continues with this newest volume set in 1944 in the United Kingdom and Wales during WWII.

In 2017, to mark the 40th anniversary of the seminal Poe Clan, “God of shojo manga” Moto Hagio released a best-selling continuation of the series. In Dream of Spring, the first volume of this new suite of tales, teen vampires Edgar and Alan are in the United Kingdom, Wales, 1944. WWII rages, and Alan is weak as they encounter figures from their past—Falka, a charismatic vampire, kind and sinister in turns; Chloe, an emissary from the Village of Poe, greedy for Edgar’s rich blood (granted by the King himself) and, above all, power; and others too mysterious to mention. Meanwhile, Edgar becomes the subject of fascination for their neighbors: 16-year-old Blanca and her little brother, Noah, Jewish refugees who long to reunite with their mother and father. Alan, dependent on Edgar and often left in the dark about vampire society, is jealous, angry, and despondent. But, for mortals and immortals alike, there are always forces (and fates) beyond their control…
products.title: The Poe Clan Vol. 3: Dream of Spring

products.body_html:
Full-color graphic novel of love and loss from the co-creator of Stigmata and The Raven.

When confronted with his girlfriend’s request that they have a child together, Samuel fled that relationship. But now, a year later, when he receives a letter from Alice announcing she is expecting a baby, old emotions flare up and he embarks on a long journey to see Alice again — to re-open, or perhaps close forever, that important chapter of his life. The Crackle of the Frost is the story of what he sees, hears, experiences, and learns during that journey.

Last year, Fantagraphics presented the extraordinary Stigmata, a stunning display of Mattotti’s whirling, emotional, black and white linework put in the service of a devastating story — as well as his painted illustrations for Lou Reed’s The Raven. The Crackle of the Frost ups the visual ante even on those masterpieces, combining the narrative drive of the former with the lush color illustrations of the latter to create a graphic-novel masterpiece with panel after panel of sumptuous full-color paintings, as if Edward Hopper had suddenly decided to jump into comics.
products.title: The Crackle of the Frost

products.body_html:
A woman wreaks havoc in Jeremy Baum’s dystopic, debut graphic novel.

Set in a dystopian future, alternating between current time and flashbacks, between an urban environment and a natural landscape, Dörfler is as much about space and time as it is about the characters who inhabit the two milieux. Strange inter-dimensional creatures live in the ancient lands of the Northern Mountains, where electronic and engine powered machinery is rendered inoperable. The city is a police state where the military subjects its citizens to experiments that turn memory and identity into malleable, political tools. While one woman wreaks havoc against the totalitarian state in revenge for what they’d done to her, two lovers wander through the Northern Mountains trying to distinguish between real and false memories. The towering landscapes, reflected in the very dimensions of the book itself, play an important role in the story—dizzying skyscrapers of rock formations and trees in contrast to the desolate, vertiginous cityscape that looks like a decaying version of Fritz Lang’s Metropolis. A bold and sure to be talked-about debut graphic novel.
products.title: Dorfler

products.body_html:
The first new edition in 30 years, I Want to Be Your Dog is the story where Ho Che Anderson announced himself as a creative force to be reckoned with.

Mary Greenberg, a Jewish Guyanese woman living in Toronto, is recovering from a bad breakup. One that makes her want to be bad all by herself. Mary's ex, Xal, is a sadomasochistic abuser and petty thief, lying low in New York City with his brother Baron. Mary was Xal's collared "dog" but this time around, she wants to be the one holding the leash. That's when she meets Damian—sweet, soft, and woefully insecure about sex. What starts as a genuine connection becomes an ugly web of moral corruption, domination, and submission. To make matters worse, Mary wants to know what it's like to kill someone. And that's before Xal washes up back in Toronto.

This new omnibus edition includes, for the first time ever in print, the digital-only short story "Miles From Home", a gently heartbreaking side sequel focusing on Mary's sister, Mo, and a brand-new chapter focusing on Mary decades later which is a bittersweet coda to the main story. Plus, bonus material featuring promotional sketches, deleted scenes, and the author's reflections on the work three decades later. Visually daring and thematically fearless, Anderson's opus remains as real and raw today.
tags: i want to be your dog omnibus
products.title: I Want to Be Your Dog Omnibus

products.body_html:
In his new memoir, collector and editor Glenn Bray focuses on the potent post-war landscape of the San Fernando Valley.

For over 50 years, Glenn Bray has been shining a spotlight on some of the most outrageous, powerful, and subversive art made in the 20th century. He was the first to preserve, collect and pay serious attention to this art, and At, With and About is nothing less than an alternative history of American pop culture.

In this compendious volume, he turns his focus on the potent post-war landscape of the San Fernando Valley's washed-up entertainers, suburbs, and Hollywood debris that lit the fuse for a life of endless aesthetic engagement. Bray met and befriended some of the most wild and woolly icons of outré culture as well as fellow travelers, collectors, and dealers that make up the world of So Cal pop history: Artists and fellow travelers such as Basil Wolverton, Carl Barks, Robert Crumb, Rick Griffin, Stanislav Szukalski, Robert Williams, Leonardo DiCaprio, Tor Johnson, The Fugs, Gorgeous George, Matt Groening, Steve Buscemi, Fred Blassie, Alfred Hitchcock, Dirty Dora, Weird Wanda, and Cash Flagg.

With all-new artist interviews and Bray's own large-format photographs, this book bears graphic witness to it all with hundreds of images tracing his life of collecting art and befriending artists.
products.title: At, With and About: Through the Blighted Lens of Glenn Bray

products.body_html: Where it all began! We are proud to present this facsimile edition of Palestine #1, originally published in early 1993 — the first appearance of Sacco’s timeless, award-winning work of comics journalism, based on his own travels in the Middle East. In this first chapter of one of the best-selling and most important graphic novels of all time, Sacco travels to Egypt and Jerusalem, hearing very different opinions of Palestine and Israel from the locals.
products.title: Palestine #1 - "Facsimile Edition"

products.body_html: Roy is haunted by nightmares of the Froat, so he gets up and goes for a stroll and runs into Tom-Jim-Jack Clown — battling a generic Froat for control of each other’s life force! In “Captain Cockatiel & Rudy,” the duo sail the high seas and discover an island of scaredy cats! Plus, Roy reveals his secrets of Christmas shopping!
products.title: Roy #2

products.body_html:
Scrupulously cataloged and profusely illustrated by master cartoonist Keith Bendis, this reimagined field guide to the 50 state birds is as elucidating as it is guffaw-inducing.

In the mid-1800s, self-made naturalist and outdoorsman John James Audubon began work on his collection of 435 watercolor plates that would become the standard-setting Birds of America. Now, some nigh on two hundred years later, its indisputable and entirely authentic successor has finally emerged.

Master cartoonist Keith Bendis has traveled to all four corners of this nation, or wishes he had, returning with accounts of the Beach Stoners of North Carolina, the Impossible Screamers of Alaska that lay eggs five times the size of their body, the "too coo for school" Red-Capped Delaware Slackers, and the alluring Pink-Breasted Frogcatcher of the Louisiana bayou.

These most whimsical and biologically unsound members of the avian species are brought to life in a style reminiscent of Gary Larson's Far Side, handsomely coupled with a rarefied New Yorker panache. Simply put, Grifters, Floaters, & Punks is essential reading for both seasoned birdwatchers and budding ornithologists as well as lovers of screwball cartooning.
products.title: Grifters, Floaters, & Punks: A Reimagined Field Guide for the 50 State Birds

products.body_html:
The most comprehensive compilation of EC Comics covers ever!

Here, for the first time, in a deluxe two-volume collection, is the best compilation of the covers from EC Comics. From the company's earliest days of its earnest Picture Stories titles to its kiddie, Western, and romance titles of the 1940s, through the heyday of such titles as Tales From the Crypt, Vault of Horror, Weird Science, Shock SuspenStories, Crime SuspenStories, Two-Fisted Tales, and Piracy, through its "New Direction" and "Picto-Fiction" period with titles such as Aces High, Extra, Impact, Terror Illustrated, and Confessions Illustrated—they're all here!

These covers were drawn by the greatest array of artistic talent ever assembled at one comic book company (excepting Fantagraphics, of course). Their names are legend—Craig, Crandall, Davis, Evans, Feldstein, Frazetta, Ingels, Kamen, Krigstein, Kurtzman, Orlando, Severin, Torres, Williamson, and Wood. And most of these covers are colored by the equally legendary Marie Severin.

Each of the hundreds of full-color covers is lovingly scanned from pristine original comics and presented in a lush, oversize format to show off with spectacular precision every meticulous line, brushstroke, and nuance of chromatographic splendor. But it doesn't end there. This unique collection also showcases alternate covers, original artwork, paperback covers — even unpublished, "what if" covers by EC "grand old man" Angelo Torres that have never seen print before.

The Crypt of Covers: The Complete EC Covers Compendium takes you on a curated tour of the history of EC Comics through its cover art from start to finish, guided by EC expert Grant Geissman. Each cover in this stunning collection is worthy of gallery or museum display.
products.title: The Crypt of Covers: The Complete EC Covers Compendium

products.body_html:
The multiple Eisner and Ignatz Award nominated comics anthology returns with its biggest issue yet! A perfect survey of the very best in contemporary art/lit-comics from around the globe.

This first new NOW of 2026 features work from several contributors familiar to NOW readers as well as others appearing in the magazine for the first time. Under an original cover by gifted Portland cartoonist Soph Franz, Kayla E. (USA) returns to NOW with an all-new memoir comic, hot on the heels of Precious Rubbish, her acclaimed 2025 graphic novel debut. NOW familiars Roman Muradov (Armenia), Josh Simmons (USA), Steven Weissman (USA), Maggie Umber (USA) and Stacy Gougoulis (Australia) are back, while Los Angeles artist Scott Marvel Cassidy contributes his first new comics since 2024's acclaimed graphic memoir Hogbook and Lazer Eyes. In "Dear Phony," Cassidy processes/confronts his own OCD in a surrealist/absurdist work worthy of and owing a debt to the works of Alfred Jarry as well as Vivian Stanshall's Sir Henry at Rawlinson's End. Meanwhile, Swedish cartoonist Iris Hautaniemi makes her NOW debut, while small press legend Zak Sally contributes a heartfelt meditation on youth and aging. All this, plus many other surprises.

NOW: The New Comics Anthology is, every issue, a self-contained cross-section of the best short comics stories the globe has to offer. The series has established itself as the preeminent anthology of first-rate international comics talent. With all-new, never before-seen material from a mix of emerging and established talent, NOW is the perfect answer to the question, "Why Comics?"
products.title: NOW #14: The New Comics Anthology

products.body_html:
Can't decide what to read? Looking for a gift, but aren't quite sure? Or do you just want to let someone buy their own damn books? Gift certificates for Fantagraphics.com are now available in four slick designs from some of our beloved cartoonists! Select your design or stick with our default design if you simply can't choose a favorite. 

You now have the choice to send a gift card to yourself or to someone else! If you send it to yourself, you'll receive an email with a confirmation and your unique gift card code. You can use the gift card yourself, forward the confirmation email or the gift card page itself to your recipient, or print it out to present in person.

If you send it to someone else, select the "Send as Gift" option and fill out the form! The gift card will be sent right to your recipient, or it can be sent on a date of your choosing.

Gift cards do not expire and can be used on any purchase, including the shipping costs.
products.title: Simon Hanselmann Fantagraphics Gift Card

products.body_html:
A giant-sized collection of original art and publisher's proofs of some of Carl Barks's most beloved stories — stunningly presented at full original art size.

Carl Barks drew these adventures of Donald Duck and Uncle Scrooge very large — "two-and-a-half times up" the size they were printed in his comic books. Now, for the first time, you can see for yourself the meticulous linework and incredible detail he lavished at the same size he worked on them at his drawing board in Carl Barks in Black and White, the second Barks focused title in our acclaimed Fantagraphics Studio Edition series.

This giant-sized special edition reproduces a goldmine of original Barks art and first-generation publisher's proofs at the artist's full original size. And when we say full size, we aren't kidding — this book measures one-and-a-half feet wide by more than two feet tall! Ideal for capturing all the detail and nuance of one of the most preeminent masters of comic art and storytelling.

We start off with three of Barks's most important and beloved stories — "In Ancient Persia," "Only a Poor Old Man," and the wacky camping adventure "Vacation Time." You'll also find in this incredible volume a complete 10-page story, lots of original covers, whole pages and panels that were cut before publication, and much, much more. Barks historian and collector Kim Weston, who spent decades patiently assembling this one-of-a-kind collection, provides important historical and artistic insight and background on how Barks produced these unforgettable gems. (Sadly, much of Barks's original art has been lost or destroyed over the years, so rare collections like this — a mix of high-resolution scans of original artwork and production proofs — take years, even decades, to bring to fruition.) An outstanding giant of a book that will constantly reward you with new discoveries every time you turn its pages.
products.title: Carl Barks in Black and White: Vacation Time and Other Stories: The Fantagraphics Studio Edition

products.body_html:
The latest volume in our Fantagraphics Atlas Creator Collection presents every single story drawn by the legendarily innovative artist in glorious and impeccably restored black and white.

While Bernard Krigstein's groundbreaking work at EC Comics has been reprinted numerous times, his substantially larger output for Atlas has been unfairly neglected. The 78 stories in this volume – the vast majority restored from original photostats – will fully rectify that oversight, and provide a greater understanding of the achievement of this often-misunderstood graphic-storytelling pioneer.

Krigstein was the only Golden Age artist with a Bachelor of Fine Arts degree, and he approached the black-and-white idiom of comics from the perspective of a student dissecting the drawings of the old masters—in this case those old masters included Jack Kirby, Mort Meskin, Alex Raymond, Jerry Robinson, and many others. Already a seasoned comic book veteran when he arrived in mid-1951, Krigstein's two-year tenure at Atlas can be seen as a vital bridge to his artistic maturity. Story by story, page by page, he stretches and refines the Atlas house style expected of its artists to its outer limits, then defies that convention to forge the personal aesthetic he'll continue to refine at EC.

After EC's collapse in 1956, Krigstein returned to Atlas to create his final body of work in comics: 29 short-form experiments demonstrating the infinite possibilities inherent in the art of graphic narrative. "I used them as a medium for dramatizing the breakdown technique, to show the limitless ways that a comic book story could unfold. I wanted to show that the form was fluid and dynamic and should not be considered a static form." Guest editor and Krigstein biographer Greg Sadowski's introductory historical essay traces the arc of Krigstein's development and his efforts to elevate the stature of a medium that was dismissed as disposable juvenile escapism.
products.title: The Atlas Creator Collection No. 4: Bernard Krigstein: The Complete Atlas Stories

products.body_html:
The tense, urban tales of Complete Mystery collected in this Atlas Library volume were among the first shots fired in what would become a veritable Timely/Atlas crime wave.

The year 1948 saw the debut of a long-form, film-noir-influenced “crime novella” comics format titled Complete Mystery featuring Marvel's top artists: Gene Colan, Syd Shores, and Carl Burgos (with three stories written by editor Stan Lee).

<[>In “Seven Dead Men!” greedy mobsters and a beautiful girl lust after a quarter of a million dollars. “Fate’s Fearful Jigsaw!” weaves a tale of murder and mystery, likely instigated by the contemporary accounts of the deaths of the famed NYC recluses, the Collyer brothers. “Fear in the Night!” has murder manifest under the big top, and a squealer causes gangland terror in “Squealers Die Fast!”

Changing to a multi-story structure, True Complete Mystery became a showcase for the earliest work by future Marvel Comics star John Buscema, who penciled four stories and a cover in the remaining four issues: “Rico Mancini – The Deadly Dude!” “Murder Will Out!” “The Frame-Up that Failed!” and the frantic “Triangle of Terror!” The final three issues sported crime-themed photo covers, a popular novelty across numerous Timely crime, romance and western titles of the period. With an historical introduction by Atlas expert Dr. Michael J. Vassallo.
products.title: The Atlas Comics Library No. 12: Complete Mystery

products.body_html:
Collected here for the first time, in a visually striking two-volume set, are the complete works of Jim Steranko at Marvel, the art and stories that dazzled readers and redefined what comic books were capable of.

Schooled in Golden Age comics, Steranko (born under the sign of Scorpio) merged pulp heroism with modern, cinematic graphic design in a way that transformed the look of Marvel's Captain America, X-Men, Daredevil, and Nick Fury, Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D. His late-1960s run on S.H.I.E.L.D. was the essence of cool, distilling the era's spy boom into a new level of sophisticated comic-book storytelling.

It's all here: all the stories (including his sole foray into the romance genre), all the cover art (including Fantastic Four, Supernatural Thrillers, Incredible Hulk Special, Shanna the She-Devil, and his variant covers for Black Panther, Civil War II, and Avengers Standoff), even his illustrations for the Marvelmania and FOOM fanzines. Every thrilling moment of the unique aesthetic marriage between Steranko and Marvel has been assembled in one place for the first time, in a gorgeously designed two-volume hardcover slipcase set.
products.title: The Marvel Creator Collection No. 2: "Whatever Happened to Scorpio?": The Complete Jim Steranko at Marvel

products.body_html: We're celebrating 50 years of publishing the world's greatest cartoonists--grab our limited edition semicentennial tote while you can! Printed by hand right here in Seattle, this sturdy, organic cotton tote features work by 14 of our most iconic artists (left to right): Laura Pérez, Alex Graham, Peter Bagge, Simon Hanselmann, Daniel Clowes, Jim Woodring, Gilbert Hernandez, Jaime Hernandez, Greg & Fake, John Pham, Roberta Gregory, Moa Romanova, and Gary Panter.
products.title: Fantagraphics 50th Anniversary Tote Bag

products.body_html:
For the first time, the entire original run of MAD comics and magazine by creator, editor, writer and cover artist Harvey Kurtzman in a lavish five-volume collector's box set, in oversized facsimile, with a wealth of bonus material.

In 1952, the first MAD comic was created as a way for the writer/editor/artist Harvey Kurtzman to do something quick and easy in between his elaborately researched war comics for EC. Against all odds, sales success soon turned it into his main job and inspired him to expand from goofy parodies of other comics into even zanier satires that revealed to the kids of America how hypocritical the adults, and entire structure of society and capitalism around them, truly were.

The core artists—Will Elder, Wallace Wood, Jack Davis and at first John Severin—all found themselves inspired by the opportunity to turn from horror or adventure comics to humor, turning out some of the best work of their comics careers – and going on to mainstream success from their name recognition MAD gave them.

By 1955, Kurtzman was ready to move on to grown-up magazine publishing—but seized an opportunity to convert MAD into a magazine first. With the same stable of artists, and a few new contributors from television (Ernie Kovacs, Roger Price), radio (Stan Freberg) and newspapers, he converted the color comic to a black-and-white magazine that aimed its satire at kids and adults alike – and went on to even greater success. Kurtzman himself, and most of his artists, moved on after five issues.

This gorgeously designed slipcase set includes the first 30 issues of MAD reprinted for the first time. Other highlights: tons of MAD original art and process work. Essays covering the history of MAD and its major players: Kurtzman, Elder, Wood, Davis, Severin, Al Jaffee, Marie Severin, William Gaines, Basil Wolverton, and Ben Oda. A section on Kurtzman's pre- and post-MAD career, covering EC, Help!, Humbug, Trump, and Little Annie Fanny/Playboy. A section on Kurtzman and Elder's unique decades-long working relationship, including a section reprinting all their work upon their short-lived return to MAD in the 1980s. Sections on MAD reprints and MAD ripoffs. A comprehensive gallery showing the various iterations of MAD cover reproductions, from the original mag to subsequent collections and archival efforts, showcasing surviving cover sketches, original cover art, color roughs, and more. Also, a short history of Alfred E. Neumann.
products.title: MAD: The Complete Harvey Kurtzman Years

products.body_html:
The second volume in a series of 10 oversized softcover editions, each one containing a half-decade's worth of Peanuts Sunday strips, elegantly restored and remastered in warm, vibrant full color.

Charles M. Schulz's beloved comic strip Peanuts has largely been collected and reprinted in black and white. But many who read the comic strip during its original newspaper run remain fond of its brightly colored Sunday pages, which made for a surprisingly different and fulfilling reading experience. Our Peanuts Every Sunday series collects all of the Peanuts Sunday strips, scrupulously restored and re-colored to look better than they ever have. These gorgeous, oversized softcover editions allow fans and new readers to immerse themselves in Schulz's timeless masterpiece.

The second volume in this series, Peanuts Every Sunday: 1956-1960, closes out the strip's early, more experimental beginnings. This collection offers a fascinating peek at Schulz's creative process, as iconic characters such as Charlie Brown, Snoopy, Schroeder, Linus, and Lucy quickly evolve from their initial renderings to the elegant stylizations we've all come to know and love.

Peanuts — beloved characters, iconic gags, drawing that finds beauty in its economic ink line. Fantagraphics is thrilled to publish Schulz's glorious creation, bringing our team's design expertise and impeccable production values to bear on the most popular comic strip of all time.
tags: schroeder lucy van pelt linus van pelt
products.title: Peanuts Every Sunday 1956-1960: Paperback Edition

products.body_html:
A double dose of Disney Duck comics adventures for the holidays!

This season's Carl Barks Library slipcased gift box set collects two of our earlier volumes in this popular series: Walt Disney's Donald Duck "Mystery of the Swamp" (Barks's first foray into his signature series of adventures in "lost civilizations'' takes the Ducks deep into the Everglades, where they find themselves bedeviled by the enigmatic Gneezles) and Walt Disney's Donald Duck: "Maharajah Donald" (Through a series of trade-ups, the nephews turn Donald's old pencil stub into — a steamship ticket to India!). More than 470 pages in two volumes snugged into a sturdy slipcase at a special price that even Uncle Scrooge couldn't resist!
products.title: Walt Disney's Donald Duck Gift Box Set "Mystery of the Swamp" & "Maharajah Donald": Vols. 3 & 4

products.body_html:
The definitive collection of comics and illustrations created by George McManus, the world-famous creator of Bringing Up Father and one of history's most popular comic strip artists. This book covers the artist's work from 1901 to 1950.

"By George" is a 500-year-old exclamation used to express astonishment; a euphemism to avoid naming a divinity. A fitting title for this collection of classic comic art—both astonishing and, in its own way, divine.

In 1913, George McManus was already a successful cartoonist with over a dozen hit comic strips to his credit. That year saw the debut of his signature creation, Bringing Up Father, soon to become an international sensation—the most popular comic strip in the world. In 1918 it appeared as a Sunday feature in full color, full-page splendor that is now, along with the artist's earlier works, recreated by Sunday Press.

This volume displays the long career of George McManus, from his early days as an artist for the St. Louis Republican, to his ground-breaking work for Joseph Pulitzer and William Randolph Hearst in New York. Early features like Panhandle Pete and Nibsy the Newsboy show McManus as one of the "Founders of the Funnies." With The Whole Blooming Family, The Newlyweds/Their Only Child, he pioneered the type of family-humor comic strip that led to the sitcoms of radio and television. This form reached a peak with the battling (yet loving) spouses, Jiggs and Maggie in Bringing Up Father.

The story behind the over 150 strips found in this collection is related in great detail by historian Paul C. Tumey in his detailed biographical introduction. McManus and his wife, even more so than his characters, were the toast of society, both at home and abroad, which added to his fame and the popularity of the strip. The book's foreword by internationally renowned cartoonist and designer Joost Swarte offers an appreciation and a description of the important influence of McManus on European artists, including Tintin's Hergé. Educator and historian Eike Exner chronicles McManus's Asian connection as one of the main American influences in the development of Manga.

Completing this comprehensive volume are photographs, illustrations, and memorabilia highlighting the long career of one of the world's greatest cartoonists—making his readers laugh at his characters (and themselves) for over half a century.

McManus has a well-deserved place in the pantheon of American cartoon artists, but never before has had a comprehensive collection of his work. Now, By George, here it is!
products.title: By George! The Comic Art of George McManus

products.body_html:
Prince Valiant's memorable cast of characters return to a corrupted Camelot as the kingdom erupts in all its savage glory.

Prince Valiant's confrontation in Iceland with merciless would-be king Eric Blacktooth culminates in a cataclysm of fire and ice. The wandering, de-throned Arthur returns to a Camelot ruled by King Ethelbert as trade imbalances threaten to plunge Europe into war. Ethelbert aims to execute Arthur with Excalibur. But as events are at their darkest, the Knights of the Round Table ride again.

Plus: Final galleries of the best images from Prince Valiant by its creator Hal Foster and his successor John Cullen Murphy, with art chosen by Prince Valiant creators and experts, including artists Gary Gianni and Tom Yeates, writers Cullen Murphy and Mark Schultz, art critic David Apatoff, and many others.
products.title: Prince Valiant Vol. 32: 1999-2000

products.body_html:
International award-winning graphic novelist Hugo Pratt's Corto Maltese returns to American readers in full color with the first volume of The Complete Corto Maltese, featuring the rip-roaring adventure that introduces him to the world.

In Fall 2026, Fantagraphics launches The Complete Corto Maltese with Volume 1: The Ballad of the Salt Sea, Corto's premiere adventure and the story that introduces him to the world. Pratt plunges us right into the action with Corto bound to a makeshift raft adrift in the Pacific Ocean in 1913. In short order, he is rescued by the Russian privateer Rasputin (yes, that Rasputin), and things only get more complicated and more treacherous from there. In addition, this volume also presents Pratt's tale of Corto's youth, when, in 1904 at the age of 16 in Manchuria, he is asked by his friend, Jack London (yes, that Jack London) to help rescue a young Russian deserter named Rasputin in the midst of the Russo-Japanese War.

A modern Ulysses whose wanderings in the early decades of the 20th century take him to the most fascinating places on Earth, Hugo Pratt's Corto Maltese is a hard-luck, hard-driving iconoclastic anti-hero who values freedom and independence more than wealth and status. Treasure hunter, storm-tossed sailor, and itinerant adventurer, the irascible and indefatigable Corto Maltese has earned his status as one of the most popular characters in European comics.
tags: fable of venice and other adventures
products.title: The Complete Corto Maltese Vol. 1: The Early Years and A Ballad of the Salt Sea

products.body_html:
The first collaboration between the legendary creative duo of Oesterheld and Breccia is an SF crime/adventure serial in which a mysterious figure saves Argentine retiree Julio Luna when a too-good-to-be-true real estate deal … is. Together, they travel through time and space, solve supernatural crimes, investigate cursed objects, and more!

In 1958, established Argentine comics creators Héctor Germán Oesterheld and Alberto Breccia worked together on their first significant series. In Sherlock Time, retiree Julio Luna buys a beautiful home for much too good a deal. There have been strange disappearances, but the trap is far stranger than a simple haunting in San Isidro. Fortunately for Luna, a mysterious man saves him in the nick of … Sherlock Time! The two team up, outwitting aliens, solving seemingly-supernatural crimes, and investigating cursed objects. These episodic adventures, ranging from SF to horror to mystery, ran concurrently with Oesterheld's legendary comics serial The Eternaut, and set the stage for their masterpiece, Mort Cinder. Of Sherlock Time, Argentine author Juan Sasturain (who also wrote Perramus, which Breccia would go on to draw) concluded: "rarely has a story made us so fully happy."
products.title: Sherlock Time

products.body_html:
An epic alternative history of colonization and industry — as only the zany, bizarre, and grotesque mind of Kago could dream up!

In Shintaro Kago's vision of history, Genghis Khan's empire was not built by soldiers and warhorses — but rather the animated severed hands of giants! From there, the history escalates at a fever pitch, as the demand for these giant hands sweeps across Asia and Europe and become indispensable for modern life as transportation, labor, power. In time, the hands mutate into other limbs and body parts and are utilized for far more destructive and sinister purposes as the world descends into a hyper capitalist, war hungry hellscape.

From the bestselling mangaka of Dementia 21 and Brain Damage comes a vicious satire of humanity's relentless greed infused with the gleeful body horror, visceral detail, and off-the-wall antics that have delighted and disgusted Kago's readers.
products.title: The Ultra Power Mongol Invasion

products.body_html:
Bouncing on the heels of Fantagraphics' first Pooh collection, the Hundred Acre Wood's famous feline gets his own comics anthology—chock-full of quests, pranks, and rootin'-tootin' adventurosity!

Do your fellow comics fans call you too flouncy and pouncy? Do fussy Rabbits see you coming and panic? Don't change your stripes, don't hide your head in a hunny pot—maybe you're a Tigger! And now you can join us for tons of Tigger comics tales, anthologized from the classic American Winnie the Pooh comic book and Disney magazines around the world!

Fronted by a feature-length adaptation of The Tigger Movie (2000), then filled up with dozens of stupendous shorts, this catty collection finds Pooh, Piglet, Roo, and Eeyore hunting Tigger's feline family members, running (and bouncing!) in marathons—even building "purrposterous" statues in ice! But the most wonderful thing about The Tiggerific Comic Collection is… it's the only one!
products.title: Winnie the Pooh: The Tiggerific Comic Collection: Winnie the Pooh Comic Book Classics Volume 2

products.body_html:
This powerful historic graphic novel highlights Spain's haunted past, small acts of resistance against fascism, and the dignity of the departed.

In the years following the Spanish Civil War, tens of thousands of Spanish civilians were unjustly executed by the brutal Franco regime. One of these poor men was José Celda, who faced the firing squad in 1940 and was buried in a mass grave in Valencia. Over seven decades later, his daughter Pepica, through years of persistence, convinces the government to exhume his grave and restore his dignity.

Amidst Pepica Celda's personal battle against oblivion, she discovers the crucial role of Leoncio Badía. The local gravedigger during those tumultuous years, Leoncio risked his life to help the widows of those killed in the war and after to identify their late husbands' bodies, record the location of their graves, and hide messages among their remains for future identification. Small acts of kindness and humanity that gave hope in a bleak era.

A powerful collaboration between the award winning cartoonist Paco Roca and notable journalist Rodrigo Terrasa, The Abyss of Oblivion is a vital work of historical memory.
products.title: The Abyss of Oblivion

products.body_html:
This haunting, nostalgic collection of short comics by Filipino American illustrator and author Bong Redila is at once an homage to childhood and a simple wish that tomorrow everything will be fine.

Welcome to Meläg. Located somewhere between dreamland and the real world of Redila's childhood hometown in the Philippines, this eerily fantastical town is where love, joy, and heartbreak hold hands. Here, a father builds a clunky wooden robot for his daughter to dance with at her wedding; a little boy rubs a mystical lamp and wishes only for a jar of sugar; a little girl finds a magical box and soars over the treetops in her tricycle; a man waits at the bus stop each day for years for his soulmate to arrive. Slices of life at turns tender and tragic that cast a kind eye toward the misunderstood and different among us.

Filipino American cartoonist Bong Redila first introduced readers to Meläg in 2022, and this new edition expands and deepens his enchanting vision with over 150 pages of new material. Drawn in a spidery, Edward Gorey-esque pen-and-ink style, this charming collection will transport readers of all ages.
tags: nocturnal whispers phantasmagoric fables from melag
products.title: Nocturnal Whispers: Phantasmagoric Fables from Meläg

products.body_html:
A giant gold nugget for Christmas, Donald heads down the river with 1,000 logs, and a race to win a kiss from Daisy — Carl Barks does it again.

Christmas isn't looking too cheerful for the citizens of Duckburg until Huey, Dewey, and Louie discover gold on Uncle Scrooge's land — but getting it out and safely to Scrooge's money bin proves to be far more complicated than anyone thought. But along the way — presents for everyone!

Then, Donald is pressured into jockeying a thousand logs down a river he's never seen to a sawmill he's never heard of — but the reward is $1.00 a log! Daring logjams, avalanches, and whirlpools, Donald and the boys risk it all — but their biggest danger comes from Black Pierre and his crew of river rats who want that reward for themselves! Next, Donald faces the greatest challenge of them all — the grueling jalopy race to fetch mistletoe from the Black Forest! The prize? The right to kiss Daisy Duck at Duckburg's Mistletoe Ball. But Gladstone Gander wants to win, too — and Gladstone's luck never fails him!

Also: A 75-page epic starring Donald and Uncle Scrooge, plus the return of the Junior Woodchucks for two adventures, both written and penciled by Barks and finished and inked by Daan Jippes.

The Good Duck Artist delivers another superb collection of surprise, delight, comedy, adventure, and all-around cartooning brilliance. 170 pages of story and art, each meticulously restored and newly colored. Bonus features include insightful story notes by an international panel of Barks experts.
products.title: Walt Disney's Donald Duck "Christmas Cheers": The Complete Carl Barks Disney Library Vol. 31

products.body_html:
A family death and a missing Picasso send a mother and son on an unexpected spring break that threatens to permanently damage their relationship — if they survive the trip!

When her semi-estranged and penniless hoarder father dies, Erin Messina is tasked with cleaning out his house before the bank forecloses on it. This otherwise thankless task is given a purpose, however, when she remembers the original Picasso drawing her father was gifted in 1964. She enlists her teenage son, Jackson, to spend spring break looking for their possible ticket to long-term financial stability. Jackson, resentful and eager to shirk responsibility, befriends twin skateboarders who live in the hood, and tell him about the violent murder that happened directly across the street from his grandfather's home — and the murderer who still lives there. Emotional baggage, paranoia, and frayed nerves stretch the Messina's relationship to the brink, as The Mess careens to a thrilling final act that includes… two-way radio communication with the dead?

Over the past decade, Noah Van Sciver has established himself as the most versatile graphic novelist working today. Whether it be in the service of straight-up satire (Fante Bukowski, Beat It, Rufus!), serious historical nonfiction (Joseph Smith and the Mormons, The Hypo: The Melancholic Young Lincoln), autobiography (As a Cartoonist, One Dirty Tree), or books for younger readers (Calamity Before Jane, Johnny Appleseed), Van Sciver's singular voice and style has proven remarkably malleable to the needs of each project. With The Mess, Van Sciver stakes yet new creative ground as a fiction writer, crafting the most magnetic and literary work of his career. The Mess is a brilliant, original graphic novel infused with drama, laughs, pathos, and suspense, beautifully drawn and colored in Van Sciver's immersive and intimate style.
products.title: The Mess

products.body_html:
2025’s Eisner Award-winning “Best Continuing Series” is back with a second technicolor tapestry of collected comic book superheroics for irreverent fans young and old!

Ambar and Alana, aka the superhero duo Santos Sisters, are back! And now, with an Eisner Award under their collective belt in addition to being imbued with the powers of the goddess Madame Sosostris, they’re even better prepared for whatever comes their way! Whether it be foiling disastrous plots to take down the local power grid, rescuing boyfriends from jealous supervillains, saving senior citizens from drug addiction, or battling the duo’s ever-expanding rogue’s gallery of supervillainery, Amber and Alana always bring the comic book fun in this healthy conflation of four-color nostalgia, action, and laughs!

Vol. 2 of Santos Sisters brings back fan-favorite foils such as Bridgette Spinner, 8-Ball, Alacran, and mean and mad Monroe, while also introducing even more abhorrent antagonists, including: the fishy Blue Agua and her Manzanillo Assassins; the punctual — and punitive —?10 O’Clock; the mysteriously dead-eyed Sergeant Murder and Agent Exeyex; and the rapaciously avaricious Billy Bitcoin! Also: Jackie Stalegum, Phantom of the Cardboard! The Numismatist! Gary Antzman! The Nature Ninjas! The Boozy Bees! Through it all, Ambar & Alana strive to maintain a healthy work/life balance, while their creators, Greg & Fake, continue their mission to revive unabashed comic book fun with this ebullient and exuberant hit indie series!
products.title: Santos Sisters Vol. 2

products.body_html:
This omnibus culls from the first 50 issues of Love and Rockets (1985–1996), presenting Gilbert Hernandez's saga of a small Latin American town, where the arrival of an assertive, sexy single mother roils the already-tempestuous lives of its residents.

Palomar is the perfect entry into the works of critically acclaimed cartoonist Gilbert Hernandez and the still-ongoing Love and Rockets comic book series! It stars the inhabitants of a small Latin American town — long-suffering midwife/sheriff Chelo; Pipo, tomboy-turned-heartthrob; Carmen, wryer than her years; teen boys Heraclio, Satch, Augustin, Jesus, Israel, and Vicente, whose paths diverge and intersect over time; Diana and Tonantzin, sisters and polar opposites; and many other finely drawn and dynamic characters — whose already-tempestuous lives are roiled when Luba, an assertive single mother, moves there to set up a bathing business.

Palomar is a selection from the first 50 issues (1985–1996) of Hernandez's multigenerational saga, which has followed the lives and loves, adventures and horrors, of his signature characters, their children, and their children's children — borne from a place where the mystical is quotidian and the quotidian is mystical — for 40+ years. These are the stories that forever changed the face (and the heart) of American comics.
products.title: Palomar: The Heartbreak Soup Stories

products.body_html:
A chance encounter in a flea market parking lot and a severed finger embroil two Vietnamese German siblings — and a vividly drawn cast of eccentric neighbors, a tough teen biker with a crush, a rollerblading girl gang, and many others — on a mission to save a desperate young Vietnamese woman from her pursuer.

Two German siblings, 12-year-old Tâm and 14-year-old Dennis Nguyen, encounter a young Vietnamese woman in trouble in a flea market parking lot. When Tâm's spy movie-obsessed schoolmate, Alex, discovers an abandoned backpack with a photo of a happy couple with Tâm's address on the back, it will lead the two to discover a severed finger. Worried, Tâm searches for the desperate woman, aided by her reluctant brother, and eventually finds Hoa Bin, who escaped from her kidnapper — who's still tracking her down. Drawn to Hoa Bin, Tâm vows to save her — even if she has to break her stern-but-loving mom's rules, dodge the bad guys in wild chases through the Berlin streets, and combine the forces of Marina, the Nguyens' tough-chick neighbor, Jutta, an elderly retired actress, a rollerblading girl gang, and many others to do so.

In Ross's empathetic, loose-but-controlled lines, cartoonishly expressive kids interact against and within the realistically depicted urban environments, given texture and grit by screen-tones. Nirvana Is Here is a contemporary crime thriller that has adventure, diasporic, coming-of-age, and love story elements, set in Berlin's working-class Lichtenberg district against a backdrop of very current social issues.
products.title: Nirvana Is Here

products.body_html:
Forming is an eon-spanning, psychedelic, metaphysical, mystical, and epic work of modern mythology and comedy: a retelling of the trajectory of consciousness on planet Earth.

In Forming, Jesse Moynihan takes 50,000 years of socio-religious postulation and throws it in the blender to create one epic—and irreverent—battle royale between alien gods, Ancient Greek Titans, interplanetary assassin droids, and humanity itself. Originally begun in 2009 and garnering hundreds of thousands of followers online, Jesse Moynihan's acclaimed Magnum Opus was never completed — until now!

Spanning Atlantis, 10,000 BC, across eons and galaxies, religions and myths, humanity emerges from the primordial soup, only to be exploited for its labor by an alien super-being, leading to wars and forces between the likes we could hardly comprehend if not given life before our very eyes via Moynihan's breathtaking and hand-painted gouache, ink, and airbrushed pages. Forming heralds the birth of civilization and maps out the genesis of life, mass, time, and space, followed by the raging war that ensues in the universe's years of adolescence and beyond, as the final fate of the universe unfolds.
